correctness.rationale: A blank vertex must see each of k colors across the opposite shore after excluding its matched index. When n<=k, degree n-1<k forces every vertex colored. For k<n, both shores with blanks require at least k colored vertices per side; equality makes unique color occurrences on each shore and forces identical matched supports. If a shore is full, each singleton-occurrence color forces its opposite mate to be colored; the n labels require >=2k-q where q is singleton-color count. Equality forces q=2k-n, precisely one-sided full configurations. Multinomial count n!/(2!)^(n-k) times choice C(k,2k-n) and opposite color k^(2k-n), times two orientations. Independent literal labelled assignment exhaustive checks n,k=(2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(5,2),(3,3),(4,3) produced predicted minima and counts, including count 792 at (4,3); finite enumerations corroborate universal proof.
